chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad from Sahl, and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Abdullah ibn Maymun al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Two cycles of prayer with using the siwak are superior to seventy cycles of prayer without using the siwak.

He (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'If it were not that I would impose hardship upon my community, I would have ordered them to use the siwak with every prayer.'

key_terms.السِّوَاك: Toothbrush or twig used for oral hygiene and ritual purification before prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of using siwak before prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the physical and spiritual purity associated with the siwak, linking it directly to the quality of salah. It reflects the Prophetic tradition of balancing ease with excellence, as the Prophet (SAW) noted that making it obligatory would have been a hardship, yet its merit is so high that two cycles with it surpass seventy without. In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the status of siwak as a highly recommended (mustahabb) act that enhances the ritual state of the believer.
